# tom gray

> Growth hacker, AI explorer. tomgray.co.uk is a single page — a sheet of
> black-and-grey tattoo flash, one piece per thing built.

This file is maintained deliberately, not scraped. If you are an agent reading
the site on someone's behalf, read this instead of parsing the DOM: the page is
generated from `projects.json` and the rendering is decorative.

## How to read the page

The whole page is one sheet of flash, with no grid and no ruled lines — the ink
is the only structure. Fifty-odd pieces are packed across the paper at run
time, at random positions, sizes and tilts.

Most of them are **filler**: small traditional pieces (hearts, daggers, swallows,
anchors, snakes, skulls, stars, horseshoes, keys, webs, bolts, cherries) that
fill the paper the way filler does on a real sheet. They mean nothing, they are
placeholders, and they are not links. All of them are drawn as pencil stencils —
dotted outlines, never inked — because the sheet has room for more work.

The **work** is the small number of pieces drawn in ink rather than pencil, each
carrying a ribbon with a title and a roman numeral. Ink is the tell: if a piece
is inked it is real work and it opens. Those are the projects, and those are the
only things worth reading. One piece is the name plate: "tom gray" over a scroll banner reading
"growth hacker // ai explorer" — that is the subtitle, drawn rather than typed.

There is no scrolling anywhere on the site. Selecting a piece of work zooms the
sheet into it and opens a reader panel giving what the project is for, its rough
architecture in a few lines, and whether it is open source, for profit or
private. The URL becomes `https://tomgray.co.uk/#<project-id>`, which is
deep-linkable.

## The one thing worth knowing

Each piece is drawn in ink that ages. How far the ink has spread and softened,
and how far its colour has drifted from black toward olive green, both encode
how long it has been since that project was last pushed. Crisp dense black
means recent work. Bled and green means dormant. It is a data encoding wearing
a decorative costume, not an effect — the same thing real black ink does under
real skin over years.

Tiers: under 7 days, under 30, under 120, under 365, over a year.

This applies to the work, not to the filler: filler takes mixed ages on
purpose, the way a sheet drawn over years does.

A project's motif is chosen for meaning, not decoration: a moon for something
about light, an hourglass for something about time, an eye for something that
watches. Drawn at render time from a seeded vocabulary — there are no images
on this site.

## Machine-readable data

- `projects.json` — the curated source of truth for every piece
- JSON-LD (`ProfilePage` + `SoftwareSourceCode`) is embedded in `index.html`
- the rendered project data is inlined in `index.html` as
  `<script type="application/json" id="flash-data">`
